title: Opened from Finder/Dock, the macOS app cannot find an installed Docker/OrbStack: SearXNG setup says 'docker CLI not found - install Docker Desktop or OrbStack' to users who have it, and the search tier stays keyless
repro: Boot the sidecar with the PATH launchd gives a GUI app (PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin; `launchctl print gui/501` has no PATH) on a Mac where OrbStack is installed and running (/usr/local/bin/docker -> OrbStack xbin/docker, vysted-searxng serving :8888) -> GET /search/searxng/status = {state:'not_installed_docker', detail:'docker CLI not found - install Docker Desktop or OrbStack', docker.cli_present:false}; Settings renders chip 'Docker not found' + 'Docker isn't available on this machine. Install Docker first' with no Set up action
evidence: lifecycle/L1-stranger/http-log.jsonl D02; lifecycle/L1-stranger.md section 4; sidecar/services/searxng_manager.py:137-144,362,420; src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:743-744,874-884; src-tauri/src/lib.rs:206-213 (sidecar spawned with args only, inherits app env; no PATH handling anywhere in src-tauri/src or sidecar/)
notes: _run_docker execs a bare 'docker' resolved through PATH. A terminal launch (tauri dev, every R15 drive) inherits a shell PATH that includes /usr/local/bin, so the defect is invisible in development; a packaged .app launched from Finder/Dock gets launchd's default PATH, where neither Docker Desktop's nor OrbStack's /usr/local/bin/docker, Homebrew's /opt/homebrew/bin nor ~/.orbstack/bin is present. Consequence: the SearXNG upgrade (the fix for SURF-FAILURE-INDUCER-2's keyless web_search timeouts) is unreachable for every macOS user who launches the app normally, and the message tells them to install software they already have. NEEDS-GUI: final confirmation on a Finder-launched packaged build; the sidecar behaviour under that PATH is measured. Smallest fix: when 'docker' is not on PATH, probe the known install locations (/usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, ~/.orbstack/bin, /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin) before reporting cli_present=false, or have the Tauri core hand the sidecar a login-shell PATH.

title: One failed rename-master fetch at boot turns the NSE rename lane off for the rest of the IST day, silently: a renamed scrip answers with its dead identity and its current ticker resolves to an unrelated US company
repro: Clean profile boot on :52225: log 'nse_symbol_change: request failed ()' then 'no file and no recent cache - rename lane is a no-op' (the URL answered 200/68,818 B in 1.35 s to a direct httpx.get a minute later). Then GET /resolve?q=GUJGASLTD -> GUJGASLTD 'Gujarat Gas Limited', former_name null, no rename note; GET /resolve?q=GUJENERGY -> needs_disambiguation led by US 'UR-ENERGY INC'. The same GUJGASLTD query on :52152 (fetch succeeded) -> GUJENERGY with note 'renamed ... effective 2026-07-01'. Further /resolve calls never retry (log still has exactly 2 nse_symbol_change lines). Mock-transport proof: first fetch ConnectTimeout -> attempts=1; 3 more schedule_refresh() -> attempts=1; only a day rollover retries.
notes: _refresh_guarded stamps _refreshed_on = today in a finally, so a failure is recorded as today's refresh and schedule_refresh (called on every /resolve) short-circuits until IST midnight. On a clean install there is no cached master to fall back to, so install day is exactly when this bites; any later day with a network blip at boot and a cache older than the stale window does the same. Nothing in /resolve, /health or the UI says the lane is off (the module calls the empty map an 'honest no-op'), and the log line carries an empty exception string with no class name (str(ConnectTimeout) is ''), so even a maintainer can't tell what failed. Distinct from SURF-ONBOARDING-STRANGER-5 (lane loaded but never fires for ZOMATO) and COD-resolver-1 (ticker-string join). Smallest fix: set _refreshed_on only on success or a successful stale-cache hydrate, retry a failure with bounded backoff, log type(exc).__name__, and expose rename_lane: unavailable on /resolve while the map is empty.

title: At boot the app starts a US-only S&P 500 warm loop every 40 s, whatever the region: on a clean first boot it opened the shared Yahoo circuit within 27 s with no user request, and at T+11 min the S&P 500 screen evaluated 0 of 506 while the India default universe ran cold in 45 s
repro: Clean keyless profile, sidecar on :52225, no user data requests for the first ~5 min: /system/provider-health yahoo open=true opens_total 1 throttles 16 at t=27 s, opens 2 / throttles 83 at 87 s, opens 4 at 357 s (CPU 41 %, RSS 393 MB on the warm cycle); log 'screener warm: rate-limited' backoff 64 -> 110 -> 227 s and 'fundamentals warm: rate-limited (streak=1); backing off 687s'. At T+11 min POST /screener/run {universe:'sp500', criteria:[pe_ratio lt 30]} -> 17.4 s, evaluated_count 0, skipped 506 all 'rate_limited', 0 results; POST {universe:'nifty50'} (the IN default) cold -> 44.8 s; opens_total 6 afterwards.
notes: _WARM_UNIVERSES = ('sp500',) is a constant and start_warm_precompute runs unconditionally in the lifespan, so an India-first install (region defaults to IN, default universe nifty50) spends its Yahoo budget pre-warming the US universe from second zero, alongside the India warm worker, on the same circuit the user's own requests use. On this run the warm never landed a cycle in 11 minutes, so it bought nothing and cost the circuit six opens. Confound: three other isolated sidecars on the same IP were warming at the same time, so the throttle speed is not a clean single-user number; the loop's region-blindness, its start-at-boot timing and the process's own throttle counters are not confounded. The panel's rendering of the 0-evaluated run is SURF-SCREENER-1 (not re-filed). Smallest fix: warm the region's default universe (nifty50 for IN), start the first cycle after a grace period or the first UI request, and keep background warming from opening the circuit user requests share.
